get.description:
Check whether the access token of the caller holds a permission, and optionally a scope, The answer comes from the verified token claims, Any caller with a valid access token can call it for their own token only

Who may call, as the spec says:
- **Permission and scope are checked separately.** `allowed` is true when `permission` is in the `permissions` claim and, when `scope` is given, `scope` is in the `scopes` claim. The claims are flat, so `allowed` does not prove that the scope was granted with that permission (Q2, Q12).
- `PLATFORM_ADMIN` gives no implicit permission: a platform administrator is allowed only what the token holds (Q3).
- Always HTTP 200 with `allowed` true or false; a permission the token does not hold is not a 403.
- No query or body parameter names another user; the answer is about the caller.

Source spec: `e-commerce/doc/api/author/17-check-permission/spec.md`

parameters.description: Permission claim to check (max 64 characters): the permission name with its last `.` replaced by `:`, lower-case letters, digits, `_` and `.`, for example `catalog:manage` or `shop.product:manage`

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Scope claim to check (max 64 characters): `<lower-case scope code>:*`, for example `all:*` or `shop:*`, Not checked when not specified

post.description:
Insert, update or delete a permission, only a platform administrator can call it, Insert when id is not specified, Update when id is specified, Delete when rowStatus is DELETED (HTTP 204 No Content, no response body), Archive when rowStatus is ARCHIVED (HTTP 200)

Who may call, as the spec says:
- `name` is the permission code: lower-case letters, digits, `_` and `.`, at least two parts separated by `.`, for example `catalog.manage` (max 64 characters) (400, E10001).
- DELETED is final: a DELETED permission is never reopened and its `id` counts as not found (404, E10004).
- A permission cannot be deleted or archived while a role (`author.t_role_permission`) or a user (`author.t_user_permission`) that is not DELETED still holds it (409, E10006).
- `scopes` lists the scopes the permission can have (`author.t_permission_scope`).

post.description:
Give a permission and its scopes to a role, change the status of the grant or take it away, only a platform administrator can call it, Insert when id is not specified, Update when id is specified, Delete when rowStatus is DELETED (HTTP 204 No Content, no response body), Archive when rowStatus is ARCHIVED (HTTP 200)

Who may call, as the spec says:
- The caller is the user of the verified access token; only a platform administrator can call this API (403, E10009).
- **The role and the permission must be ACTIVE only when the request gives the permission**, that is an insert, or an update that sets `rowStatus` ACTIVE on a row that is not ACTIVE, otherwise 404 (E10005).
- A role can have a permission once among the rows that are not DELETED (409, E10003).
- `scopes` are the scopes the role gets for this permission (`author.t_role_permission_scope`); each `scopeId` must be a scope of the permission (`author.t_permission_scope`), otherwise 400 (E10001). Scopes that are not listed are kept.
- **A scoped permission needs a scope.** After the whole request, an ACTIVE grant of a permission that has scopes must have at least one ACTIVE scope, otherwise 400 (E10001) and the request is rolled back.

- The rules of this section, including the permission model (the fixed shop roles OWNER, ADMIN and STAFF or a platform administrator, 403 E10009), were approved by the product owner.
- A member of a shop is a user that has a row in `shop.t_shop_user` with the role OWNER, ADMIN or STAFF that is ACTIVE, in a shop that is ACTIVE. The queries "Check shop member" and "Check shop members" of the shop product SKU APIs use this definition. INACTIVE, LOCKED, ARCHIVED and DELETED rows are not members. The caller is the user of the access token, never a field of the request.

An OWNER of the shop or a caller with the exact case-sensitive role `PLATFORM_ADMIN` in the verified `roles` claim (an array of role names, an empty array is valid) can add members and can change the role or the row status of every member, also of the other owners. An ADMIN of the shop can add a STAFF member and can change or remove a shop user whose role is STAFF before and after the change; adding, changing or removing an ADMIN or an OWNER is 403 (E10009). An ADMIN or a STAFF member can delete or archive their own membership (leave the shop); a caller that is only a STAFF member can only delete or archive their own membership, every other change is 403 (E10009). A platform administrator that is not a member of the shop is not counted in the OWNER rule below. The platform administrator is read only from the verified `roles` claim: do not query `author.m_role` or `author.t_user_role`, a change of the role assignments does not change a token that was already issued. Membership of a shop is not a token claim and is still read from `shop.t_shop_user`.
- The shop must keep at least one OWNER that is ACTIVE; this rule replaces the former rule of at least one ACTIVE ADMIN. A request that leaves the shop without one is rejected with 409 (E10006): this covers deleting or archiving the last OWNER, changing it to ADMIN or STAFF, setting it to INACTIVE, LOCKED or ARCHIVED, and leaving the shop, so an OWNER can leave the shop or change their own role only while another ACTIVE OWNER remains. A platform administrator cannot skip this rule. The rule is checked on the state after the whole request is applied, and the whole request is rolled back when it fails.

bearerAuth.description: Access token from POST /v1/auth/login or POST /v1/auth/refresh-token, sent as `authorization: Bearer <token>`. A valid signature and expiry are not enough. After them the API also checks that the hash of the exact token matches an ACTIVE stored credential and that the user is ACTIVE; a token that was logged out, replaced by a refresh or closed by a password reset is refused with 401 (E10002). Roles come only from the `roles` claim of the verified token (a platform administrator has the exact, case-sensitive role `PLATFORM_ADMIN`), never from the database.
